key_insight: SPG-Layout improves text-driven indoor scene synthesis by combining statistical object priors with a hierarchical placement strategy to better handle non-Manhattan spatial geometry.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for simulation, digital twins, and generative design workflows that need physically plausible room layouts in irregular architectural spaces.
method: Use statistical priors of object distributions to guide training and improve environmental fidelity.
Place large objects first in a hierarchical layout pipeline to reduce geometric violations.
Generate scenes that balance semantic realism with physical plausibility in non-orthogonal environments.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate on a new benchmark of 500 diverse non-Manhattan environments and report consistent gains over existing methods in both Manhattan and non-Manhattan settings.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the learned priors and the diversity of the training/evaluation environments, especially for unusual room geometries.
paper_title: Text-Driven 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis in Non-Manhattan Environments
